requirements.title: Lead in children's jewellery
evidence: Lab test report per accessible component - each charm, clasp, bead, plating and solder joint
requirements.plain_english: Jewellery made for children 12 and under is a children's product, and the lead limits apply to each accessible component rather than to an average of the piece. Testing a composite sample is the classic mistake here - it dilutes a non-compliant clasp or solder joint into a passing number.
requirements.self_check_hint: Get results component by component, not one figure for the item. Ask specifically about the clasp, the solder, the plating and any painted or coated bead.

requirements.title: Cadmium limits are state law, not one federal rule
evidence: Cadmium test results where a state limit applies
A record of which states you sell into
requirements.plain_english: There is no single federal cadmium limit covering all jewellery. Several states set their own numerical limits, and the widely quoted 100 ppm figure comes from a standard and from state law rather than from one federal rule. CPSC can still act where a product presents a hazard, but that is a different route with a different test.
requirements.self_check_hint: Check which states you actually sell into and what each requires, rather than applying one remembered number. If a supplier cites 100 ppm, ask which authority they mean.

requirements.title: Gold, silver and gemstone claims
evidence: Quality mark accompanied by a maker's trademark or name
Substantiation for fineness, plating thickness and gemstone descriptions
requirements.plain_english: If you describe an item as gold, silver, platinum, plated or gemstone-set, the description has to be accurate and the terms have specific meanings. Solid, vermeil, filled, bonded, plated and flashed are not interchangeable. A quality stamp also has to be accompanied by a maker's mark - a fineness stamp on its own is not enough. Laboratory-grown and treated stones have to be disclosed as such.
requirements.self_check_hint: Read your listing title and bullets as claims. Check any quality stamp is paired with a trademark, and that plated goods are not described in a way that implies solid metal.
